A bug-fix release. Two independent faults were losing releases from the One Pace
feed — one dropped them before downloading, the other lost the file afterwards.
Together they explain a whole batch of episodes going missing.

## Fixed

- **Whole-arc batch releases were silently dropped.** One Pace distributes most
  arcs as a *single folder torrent* — `[One Pace][1-7] Romance Dawn [1080p]` —
  with no CRC32 in the torrent name, the magnet, or anywhere else, and a feed
  title that is just the arc name. With no episode number to parse and no hash to
  resolve, those entries were logged as unparseable, marked as seen, and **never
  retried** — losing the entire arc. That's **21 of the 37 arcs**, including
  Marineford, Dressrosa and Whole Cake Island, so this was the normal case
  failing rather than an edge case. Such a title is now resolved as an arc and
  queued as one batch download; every episode in the folder is then imported by
  its own CRC32.

- **"Downloaded file not found in /downloads" after a successful download.** The
  completed-file lookup only searched the top level of the download directory and
  one folder below it. qBittorrent nests deeper whenever a category is
  configured — `<downloads>/<category>/<arc folder>/<episode>.mkv` for a batch —
  so the file was invisible and the import failed even though the bytes were on
  disk. The lookup and the batch-sibling scan now walk the tree to a bounded
  depth, covering every qBittorrent layout.

- **Washed-out thumbnails are now actually caught.** The clipped-pixel test added
  in 1.1.27 used a single 92% cutoff and the real offender measured 89%.
  Measuring a full library showed one cutoff can't work: genuinely detailed
  bright frames reach 80%+ clipped while carrying a very wide colour spread.
  Detection now combines both signals, so washed-out frames are regenerated while
  real high-contrast stills are left alone.

- **The OnePacerr source ignored archived releases.** Its `files` map holds a
  single object for `standard`/`extended` but an **array** for `archived`, so
  every superseded release was skipped and an older file on disk could not be
  resolved through that source.

## Upgrading

After updating, use **Retry failed** — anything that failed with the
"file not found" error should import straight from the existing download rather
than downloading again. Feed items dropped by the first bug were already marked
as seen, so re-run **Refresh Sources** to pick up whatever is still in the feed.

## Docker

```
docker pull ghcr.io/dyonng/one-pace-plex-automator:1.1.30
```
